facts.statement: Cerasinops was a small ceratopsian dinosaur.
facts.quote: Cerasinops (meaning 'cherry face') was a small ceratopsian dinosaur.

facts.statement: Cerasinops lived during the Campanian stage of the late Cretaceous Period.
facts.quote: It lived during the Campanian of the late Cretaceous Period.

facts.statement: Fossils of Cerasinops have been found in the Two Medicine Formation in Montana.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found in Two Medicine Formation, in Montana.

facts.statement: Cerasinops was named and described by Brenda Chinnery and Jack Horner in 2007.
facts.quote: Cerasinops was named and described by Brenda Chinnery and Jack Horner in 2007

facts.statement: The holotype specimen indicates a total body length of 2.5 meters and a body mass of 175 kilograms.
facts.quote: indicating a total body length of 2.5 m and a body mass of 175 kg.

facts.statement: Cerasinops is classified as a basal member of Neoceratopia, though its exact placement within the group is variable.
facts.quote: Within this group, it has been placed as a basal member of Neoceratopia, although the description is variable

facts.statement: Cerasinops has been assigned to the family Leptoceratopsidae, considered a sister taxon to that family, or placed generally within Neoceratopia.
facts.quote: at one point, it is explicitly assigned to Leptoceratopsidae, but in others, it is considered a sister taxon to Leptoceratopsidae, or as a neoceratopsian in general.

facts.statement: The species name hodgskissi honors Wilson Hodgskiss, the landowner where the specimen was discovered.
facts.quote: The species name is in honor of Hogdskiss who owned the land the specimen was found on.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MOR 300 preserves about 80% of the skull and skeleton, including most limbs but excluding the hands and tail.
facts.quote: MOR 300 preserved about 80% of the skull and skeleton in association, with much of the skull and vertebrae except the tail, both forelimbs except the hands, and most of the left and some of the right hindlimb.

facts.statement: All known specimens of Cerasinops come from the lower Two Medicine Formation, dated between 77 and 80.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: All specimens of Cerasinops are from the lower Two Medicine Formation, between Campanian ash beds that are dated at 77 and 80.2 million years ago.

facts.statement: Cerasinops is classified within the family Leptoceratopsidae.
facts.quote: familia: Leptoceratopsidae

facts.statement: Cerasinops hodgskissi is the only known species in the extinct genus Cerasinops, a leptoceratopsid ceratopsian dinosaur.
facts.quote: Cerasinops hodgskissi (gr. «cara de cereza de Wilson Hodgskiss») es la única especie conocida del género extinto Cerasinops dinosaurio ceratopsiano leptoceratópsido

facts.statement: Cerasinops measured approximately 1.70 meters in length and 0.90 meters in height, with an estimated weight of 13 to 18 kilograms.
facts.quote: Cerasinops medía aproximadamente 1,70 metros de largo y 0,90 de alto, con un peso estimado de 13 a 18 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Cerasinops had a wide, thick skull with a parrot-like beak ending in a strong rim.
facts.quote: Su cráneo, ancho y grueso, presentaba en un pico similar al de los loros actuales, el cual terminaba en un fuerte reborde.

facts.statement: Cerasinops possessed an extra tooth at the front of the jaw and a unique chewing method compared to Asian and North American ceratopsians.
facts.quote: De los primeros posee un diente extra en el frente de la mandíbula y de los segundos, una manera única de masticar.

facts.statement: Paleontologists debate whether Cerasinops is a basal ceratopsian or a sister taxon to the family Leptoceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Esta clasificación está en discusión por varios paleontólogos, que si bien lo consideran un ceratopsio basal, piensan que es un taxón hermano de Leptoceratopsidae.

facts.statement: Cerasinops lived approximately 80 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the late Cretaceous in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 80 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Fossils of Cerasinops were discovered by Jack Horner in 1983 and described by Brenda Chinnery in 2007.
facts.quote: Los restos fósiles del Cerasinops fueron descubiertos por Jack Horner en 1983 y descritos por Brenda Chinnery en el 2007

facts.statement: The parent group for the genus Cerasinops is Leptoceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Leptoceratopsidae

facts.statement: The time range for the genus Cerasinops is estimated from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The genus name Cerasinops translates to 'face of cherry,' referencing the color of the fossil-bearing beds.
rejected.quote: The genus name is from the Latin word cerasinus and suffix -ops, translating as 'face of cherry' in reference to the color of the beds and fossils
